subject: Payment rhythm exception request — Bridgestone
body:
-----Original Message-----
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Ellie Harris <ellie.harris@bridgestone.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Payment rhythm exception request — Bridgestone

Hi Ellie / Team,

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Bridgestone is formally requesting a shift from our standard monthly invoicing to a quarterly invoicing cadence for the enterprise contract tied to deal BRG-2026-041. They want invoices issued at the end of each quarter, with a 30-day payment window after invoice date (effectively Net-60 from milestone completion in some cases).

Key asks from Bridgestone (summarized):
- Quarterly invoicing (Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct) instead of monthly
- Consolidated invoice per quarter covering multiple project milestones
- Ability to submit a single PO per quarter (procurement@bridgestone.com attached a template)
- No change to pricing; early-pay discounts not requested

Attached: Bridgestone_PO_Req.pdf (procurement template), bridgestone-quarterly-schedule.csv (their proposed invoice dates).

I don’t have authority to approve non-standard invoicing cadence — looping in Marissa and Jonas for deal-desk/exec approval and Karthik for finance/process impact review. Bridgestone is asking for an answer by Friday to meet their procurement cycle.

Questions for approvers:
- Any blocking compliance or collections concerns with quarterly consolidated invoices?
- Do we need a short-term credit hold or prepay requirement before we shift cadence?
- If approved, what contract language/PO clause should we require to limit risk?

Thanks,
Soojin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com


On Tue, 10 Nov 2026 at 18:05, Ellie Harris <ellie.harris@bridgestone.com> wrote:
> Hi Soojin —
>
> Thanks for routing. A couple clarifications from procurement so you have the exact ask:
> - They will only issue four POs per year (quarterly). Each PO will reference the master agreement and list line items for the quarter.
> - Payment owners want invoices consolidated to reduce AP overhead; they will still pay within 30 days of invoice receipt.
> - There may be occasional timing mismatches if a milestone finishes a few days after quarter close — their AP is comfortable paying within 30 days of the invoice date rather than milestone date.
>
> Attached the procurement template. Let me know if you need a short justification memo for their internal approvers.
>
> Best,
> Ellie Harris
> Sr. Procurement Manager — Bridgestone Global
> procurement@bridgestone.com


On Wed, 11 Nov 2026 at 08:17, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the context, Soojin and Ellie.
>
> A few quick notes from finance/ops perspective:
> - Quarterly invoicing is doable but increases our collections exposure and working capital needs. We typically require a PO per invoice and an explicit acceptance clause tying invoice amount to delivery milestones.
> - For enterprise exceptions, we ask for either a 10% upfront prepay per quarter OR a short-term credit line confirmation (internal credit approves) to cover a single-quarter gap.
> - We also need the contract to include a clause that allows us to invoice monthly in the event of missed payment or credit deterioration.
>
> Can Karthik run an estimate of the DSO impact if we shift this account to quarterly invoices at the current T&Cs? If the DSO/working-capital hit is within our tolerance and procurement signs the master PO, we can provisionally approve with the prepay or credit-confirmation requirement.
>
> -Marissa
> Head of Revenue Ops | Redwood Inference
> marissa_cole@redwood.com


On Wed, 11 Nov 2026 at 09:02, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Running numbers now — preliminary: moving Bridgestone to quarterly invoicing increases DSO by ~28 days on average and would require ~1.2M of incremental working capital on a run-rate basis (assuming current usage and billing levels).
>
> If we require a 10% prepay per quarter, the working-capital exposure drops to ~0.3M; if procurement can supply a credit confirmation/letter of guarantee we could lower exposure further.
>
> I'll finalize the cash-impact numbers by EOD and flag any ledger/AR system constraints (we may need to adjust billing workflows since consolidated invoices with multiple milestones require a slightly different invoice numbering flow).
>
> -Karthik
> Senior Finance Manager | Redwood Inference
> karthik_iyer@redwood.com


On Thu, 12 Nov 2026 at 10:03, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com> wrote:
> Conditional approval from me to support the enterprise procurement timeline, subject to the following firm conditions:
>
> 1) Bridgestone provides a signed quarterly PO for each quarter in advance of us shipping any billable milestones for that quarter OR provides a formal credit confirmation from their bank/credit officer.
> 2) We include a contract clause limiting the exception to 12 months and an automatic reversion to monthly invoicing if any payment is >45 days overdue.
> 3) 10% prepay per quarter is preferred; if Bridgestone cannot prepay, we will accept the credit confirmation route but require AR to run weekly reconciliations for their account in the first two quarters.
>
> If these conditions are acceptable, instruct legal to add the exception language and finance to prepare the revised AR workflow. Please confirm and copy me on the PO/credit confirmation when received.
>
> Jonas Weber
> VP Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
> jonas_weber@redwood.com


On Thu, 12 Nov 2026 at 11:08, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Jonas — will proceed with the conditional approval path.
>
> Ellie — Bridgestone can proceed with either: (A) signed quarterly POs in advance, or (B) a bank credit confirmation + weekly reconciliations for first two quarters. If you can do a 10% prepay each quarter that’s preferred and will simplify setup.
>
> I’ve asked legal to stand by for the contract language and looped finance to queue AR changes. Attaching the procurement template again for your PO team.
>
> Next steps:
> - Ellie to confirm which of the three options Bridgestone will provide (PO / prepay / credit confirmation) by Friday 11/13.
> - Legal to prepare 12-month exception language and auto-revert clause.
> - Karthik to deliver final DSO/working-capital impact memo by EOD.
>
> I’m copying Marissa and Jonas here — will update once Bridgestone confirms.
>
> Thanks,
> Soojin
>
> Attachments: Bridgestone_PO_Req.pdf, bridgestone-quarterly-schedule.csv
